- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% to avoid undershoot.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 3–5 days to prevent overreaction.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.77) and price is falling, model often underestimates the decline; add 1–3% to forecast to reflect mean reversion toward prior range.
- Model frequently underestimates long-term (30d) declines when sentiment is mixed or negative; apply a 1–4% upward bias to forecast if sentiment <0.50 over last 7 days.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.27–0.80), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values before applying trend correction.
- If model forecast is >10% above true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, apply downward correction by 1–3% per day to avoid persistent overestimation.
- For sentiment history with high variance, reduce forecast volatility by 20–40% of standard deviation to match observed price stability.
